findings: The pinned fundamental keymap binds Ctrl+N to forward-line and Ctrl+A to beginning-of-line; the DEL key binding invokes backdel.
backdel moves backward one character through backchar and then deletes one logical character. At offset zero on the second line, backchar moves to the previous line's end.
ldelete detects zero remaining bytes on the current line and calls ldelnewline, joining that line to the next without dropping either line's text.

The fixture is exactly first newline second newline. One Backspace at the start of the second line therefore produces firstsecond newline; the contract asserts the screen, saves, exits, and checks exact bytes.

The first native attempt on both hosts passed the joined-text screen checkpoint and saved, but the save status clipped the filename because the hosted workspace path exceeded the viewport. The original full-basename confirmation timed out; the revised contract checks the visible Wrote prefix and retains the exact final file-state assertion.
